speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of high fever, seizure, and a non-pruritic rash. To understand the cause, have you experienced any recent tick bites, mosquito exposure, or travel to tropical regions?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum). The clinical presentation of a high fever followed by a rash after the fever breaks, in a 9-month-old with a recent seizure, is classic for this viral exanthem.
